facts.text: The first upgrade of Street Fighter II, released in 1992. In Japan it's Street Fighter II Dash.
The first time you could play the four bosses: Balrog, Vega, Sagat and M. Bison.
It added the series' first mirror matches. The copy's colours depend on which button you pick with.
Combos weren't planned. Lenient timing let special moves cancel normal hits, and designer Akira Nishitani kept it as a feature.
In Japan the boxer is M. Bison, a nod to Mike Tyson. Abroad, three boss names were shuffled, reportedly to avoid a lawsuit.
Designed by Akira Nishitani and Akira "Akiman" Yasuda, produced by Yoshiki Okamoto.
About 140,000 cabinets sold in Japan alone, numbers a Capcom developer called "unheard of".
Fireball (Ryu, Ken): roll down to forward, then punch. Directions flip when you switch sides.
Classic Ryu or Ken combo: jumping heavy kick, crouching medium kick, then fireball.
Hold away from your opponent to block, and down-away to block low attacks.
